report.math_notes: Checked every step of the argument as an adversarial reader. Lemmas 1–3 (recursion p(v)=[valley]+Σ_{u→v}p(u); p(v)≥max(1,deg^-(v)); T=|E|+v+X with X=Σ_edges(p(tail)−1)≥0) are correct and complete. Lemma 4 (light vertex ⇒ valley or in-degree 1 with light in-neighbour; light sets induce forests, via the max-label vertex of a cycle having two in-neighbours) is correct. Lemma 5: for heavy u with in-degree i∈{1,..,4}, c(u)=(5−i)(p(u)−1) with p(u)≥i; the four cases give c≥4,≥3,≥4,≥3 respectively, so c≥3, and c=3 iff (i,p)∈{(2,2),(4,4)}; the i=1 case correctly forces a second heavy vertex. Lemma 7 (in-degree sum 80=5q+s_H+(32−q−|H|−v)) is correct: peaks, heavy vertices and valleys are pairwise disjoint (peak has deg^-=5 so p≥5; heavy needs deg^+≥1; valley has p=1), and every remaining vertex is light with in-degree exactly 1. Case analysis for T≤87 (v+X≤7, X≤6, |H|≤2): |H|=2 forces X=6, v=1, s_H∈{4,6,8}, 4q∈{47,45,43} – impossible; |H|=0 forces v=4, q=13, T=84; |H|=1 forces (i,v,q,T)∈{(2,1,12,84),(3,2,12,86),(4,3,12,86)}; all residues and inequalities re-verified. Reduction to (★) (independent 12-set I, u∉I, Q_5−(I∪{u}) a forest) is valid, including the A-case trick of removing one peak. The finite reduction by XOR-translations is justified (vertex-transitive automorphisms, (★) automorphism-invariant); the backtracking prunes only by remaining-vertex count (trivially sound); acyclicity criterion |E|=|V|−#components is exact. Independent hand check of the count: independent 12-sets of Q_5 are 2·C(16,12)=3640 one-class sets plus 16+16 mixed sets (|A|=1 or |B|=1, since two same-class vertices forbid ≥8 of the other class), total 3672, matching the script and 3672·12/32=1377. Orchestrator re-runs confirm 0 acyclic complements over all 27540 (resp. 73440) pairs, so T≥88. Upper bound: the labelling was checked by hand (R={00000,11110} at distance 4, disjoint neighbourhoods, F a forest with 18 vertices/10 edges/8 components; valleys 1–8 have all neighbours higher; leaves 9–18 have exactly one lower neighbour; peaks 19–32 have all 5 neighbours odd with p=1) giving 18+14·5=88, and confirmed by two independent exact scripts re-run by the orchestrator. The labelling is given in the required 32-string format. Conclusion U(Q_5)=88 is established; the lower bound depends on the exact exhaustive computation (code_2/code_3, <1 s, outputs confirmed by trusted observations), with the reduction to that finite set fully proved in the text. Consistency: the same framework reproduces U(Q_4)=34 (3q=16+v) and the known impossibility of 81 for Q_5 (4q=49).
